title: Stream isolation and dynamic kernel variant selection for stable CUDA graph replay
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: We see intermittent correctness regressions and non-deterministic token misalignment after CUDA graph replay when multi-stream decode runs concurrently and kernel selection differs between capture and replay. Root causes observed include: (1) kernel variant chosen at capture time optimized for a specific sequence-length/hardware pairing that is incompatible when request batch shapes change at replay; (2) shared allocator and small-buffer coalescing between streams leading to different memory layouts that trigger divergent code paths; (3) racey heuristics in the capture path that prune kernel fallback paths to save capture time, causing hard failures on replay. Goal: implement a layered solution that (a) isolates capture metadata per stream and records a small deterministic kernel-selection fingerprint, (b) introduces a lightweight kernel-variant reconciliation phase at replay that either rebinds to compatible variants or triggers a fast safe fallback (no-graph path) with minimal latency penalty, and (c) adds deterministic golden-trace tests and stress harness to validate correctness across shape permutations and preemption scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: No token misalignment or output diffs > 1e-6 across 100k randomized multi-stream replay trials using the new fingerprint + reconciliation flow
Mean additional tail latency for reconciliation path < 4ms P95 under typical burst conditions on our p4d-like fleets
Automatic safe fallback to non-graph decode occurs on first detected incompatibility and is recorded in trace logs; no request is dropped
New unit and e2e tests covering: sequence-length drift, batch-shape permutations, allocator layout changes, and preemption-induced kernel rebinds
Feature gated and rolled out behind runtime-1.20 feature flag with telemetry capturing reconciliation hits and fallback counts
plan: Design: define a compact kernel-selection fingerprint (hash of kernel-id + shape-class + quantization-mode + allocator-tag) and attach to graph capture metadata
Engineering: implement per-stream capture headers that do not share allocator transient state; move small-buffer pooling to stream-local arenas during capture windows

Reconciliation: implement replay-time validator that compares fingerprint; if mismatch, attempt to find a compatible kernel variant via a prioritized lookup table keyed by shape-class and hardware capabilities
Fallback: implement a single-request fast path that disables graph replay (falls back to dynamic kernel invocation) and re-queues a background job to attempt safe re-capture after traffic quiesces
Testing: build golden-trace corpus from representative traffic (short/long prompts, multi-turn chat, embeddings interleaved) and add CI job that runs randomized permutation replay matrix nightly
Observability: add metrics/trace fields: graph_capture_fingerprint, reconciliation_attempts, reconciliation_success, graph_fallback_reason, fallback_duration_ms
Rollout: feature-flag behind runtime-1.20, start Canary group on Dedicated fleet, monitor reconciliation/fallback rate for 48h before broad rollout
comments: 2026-02-19 — Initial triage: reproduced misalignment locally with synthetic two-stream burst using seq-len drift +-8. Root cause narrowed to kernel variant mismatch during replay. (Asha)
2026-02-25 — Prototype fingerprint implemented; microbench shows 0.8ms median cost to compute and attach to capture metadata. Performance impact acceptable. (Marco)

2026-03-01 — Integration test: when replay picks different kernel, we observed a 0.02% diff in outputs due to kernel numeric edge-cases on fp16 matmul. Decided to treat numeric-unstable kernel variants as incompatible and force fallback. (Discussion in sync)

2026-03-03 — Design review notes: prefer prioritized lookup instead of brute force rebind to limit replay-time jitter. Action: create kernel compatibility table and expose it to runtime via static JSON shipped with binary. (Design/Eng)

2026-03-07 — Stress-run: 10k replay permutations with preemption; reconciliation succeeded 98.7% of the time, 1.3% caused safe fallback. Need to investigate allocator-related fallbacks — allocator arena tagging was missing for some legacy paths. (QA)
2026-03-09 — PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5123 — implements fingerprint compute, per-stream arenas, and reconciliation lookup. Requesting review from @leah and @samir. (Marco)

2026-03-10 — Added golden-trace CI job and dashboard: grafana.redwood/apps/cudagraphs/reconciliation. Telemetry shows reconciliation_success at 98.6% on canary. Next: reduce fallback rate by addressing allocator tagging. (Asha)
